CASE: Jeffrey Fouse and Brianna Miller v. E. Mishan & Sons, Inc., Riverside County Superior Court CVRI2505343. Complaint filed Sep 8, 2025 (Settlement Agreement p.1). Settlement filed May 28, 2026. Preliminary approval order dated Jul 6, 2026.

PRODUCTS: 'all Gotham Steel, Granite Stone, and Bell & Howell brand cookware products with stainless steel components' (Agreement, definition K).

CLASS AND MONEY: CA or CO purchasers, not for resale, Sep 8, 2021 to Jul 6, 2026. $6 per product, up to 2 per household ($12). Claim, opt-out and objection deadline Sep 25, 2026 (passed).

HEARING: Final Approval Hearing 8:30 a.m. Nov 2, 2026, Dept 1, 4050 Main St, Riverside (Long Form Notice Q21).

ALLEGED MARKETING: 'Healthy, Non-Toxic Ceramic Cookware & Bakeware', 'Non-toxic', 'Safe', 'Free from PFOA, PFOS, PTFE, BPA, lead, and cadmium', 'Toxin Free', 'PFOA Free', despite the undisclosed presence of chromium, iron, nickel, lead, cadmium, PFOA, PFAS, PTFE or PFOS.

COURT STATUS: No physical injury alleged. Defendant denies. 'The Court did not rule in favor of either side.'

LABEL CHANGE, VERIFIED in the Settlement Agreement section B 'Changes to Advertising & Marketing': within 180 days after the Effective Date, conform to Cal. Health & Safety Code 109011. Labels and the online product page must read 'This product contains: iron, chromium, and nickel', plus an English/Spanish line 'For more information about chemicals in this product, visit' with a URL and QR code. Expires after 3 years or a change in law. The Long Form Notice Q7 confirms it. Topclassactions (Sep 3, 2026) also reports it.

CPSC (SaferProducts.gov recall API): recall 26377 dated 2026-04-02, 'E Mishan Recalls Granitestone Diamond Pro Blue Stainless Saute Pans Due to Impact and Burn Hazards'. Hazard: the metal cap on the screw connecting the pan to the handle can detach and forcefully eject when heated. Importer: E Mishan & Sons, Inc., New York. URL: https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2026/E-Mishan-Recalls-Granitestone-Diamond-Pro-Blue-Stainless-Saute-Pans-Due-to-Impact-and-Burn-Hazards

SOURCES: https://www.stainless-steelcookwaresettlement.com/ (plus /assets/uploads/settlement-agreement.pdf and long-form-notice.pdf), https://topclassactions.com/lawsuit-settlements/open-lawsuit-settlements/bell-howell-pfas-cookware-class-action-settlement/

original_spec.title: Is LiLash Safe? What a New Lawsuit Says Is Hiding in the Serum (2026)
original_spec.villain: Cosmetic Alchemy LLC, maker of LiLash and LiBrow. A lawsuit says it sold $90 to $150 'natural' serums containing a drug-class ingredient it did not disclose.
original_spec.receipt: Meyers v. Cosmetic Alchemy LLC, Case No. 2:26-cv-09703 (C.D. Cal.), complaint filed 08/31/26 (https://www.classaction.org/media/meyers-v-cosmetic-alchemy-llc-complaint.pdf); news summary from ClassAction.org, Sept 30, 2026 (https://www.classaction.org/news/class-action-lawsuit-claims-lilash-librow-serums-contain-unsafe-drug-ingredient). The complaint ALLEGES that LiLash Purified Eyelash Serum and LiBrow Purified Eyebrow Serum contain dehydrolatanoprost, a prostaglandin analog (PGA) in the same class as the active ingredient in Rx-only Latisse. It ALLEGES the ingredient is placed at the bottom of the ingredient list with no explanation, and that the company did not disclose the risks: blepharitis, Meibomian gland dysfunction, chronic dry eye, redness, discoloration and more. It ALLEGES the serums were sold as 'natural' and 'safe for sensitive' eyes to thousands of buyers at about $90-$150 each, and cites the EU Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety's concerns about PGAs in cosmetics. There is no ruling yet. Say 'the lawsuit claims', not that the company hid the ingredient.

topics.title: Is Al Fresco Chicken Sausage Recalled? What Is on the Kayem Recall List (2026)
topics.angle: It is in her freezer for quick weeknight dinners, and she picked it because the package said chicken and all natural. Is the sausage, deli turkey or holiday ham in her fridge on the list, and did she already feed it to her family?
topics.facts: USDA FSIS Recall 026-2026, announced Oct 17, 2026 (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFSIS/bulletins/42f8d37). Class I. Kayem Foods Inc. (Chelsea, MA) is recalling about 1,584,361 pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry produced about Mar 31 to Oct 7, 2026, for possible temperature abuse in a warehouse cooler. The establishment marks inside the USDA inspection seal are EST. M/P 7839, P 20935A and M 9520. No illnesses are confirmed. Food Safety News, Oct 17, 2026 (https://www.foodsafetynews.com/2026/10/more-than-1-5-million-pounds-of-hot-dogs-bacon-sausage-turkey-breasts-and-more-meat-products-of-various-brands-recalled/): the problem was found after a retail customer reported warm product on Oct 1. Products include hot dogs, bacon, sausage, turkey breasts and hams. Fox 32 Chicago, Oct 18, 2026 (https://www.fox32chicago.com/news/1-5-million-pounds-meat-pork-products-sold-nationwide-recalled): items under Al Fresco and McKenzie were pulled. NBC News Select, Oct 20, 2026 (https://www.nbcnews.com/select/shopping/kayem-meat-products-recall-2026-rcna604639): names chicken sausage, turkey breast and corned beef. Kayem consumer line: 800-426-6100. NOT YET CONFIRMED: the exact Al Fresco item names and UPCs, because the FSIS product list PDF returns 403 to fetch tools. Triple M and Deutschmacher are also unconfirmed as recalled brands.
topics.must_fix: Before writing, open the FSIS product list PDF in a real browser and copy the exact Al Fresco item names, UPCs and dates. If no Al Fresco item is on it, retitle to 'Kayem Recall List 2026: ...' (the slug already fits). Name Triple M or Deutschmacher only if the PDF lists them. Leave out the plant's earlier recall history unless the FSIS archive confirms it. Say plainly that there are no confirmed illnesses. Say 'may have experienced temperature abuse', never 'spoiled'. USDA is the source of the fact, not a safety stamp for other meat. 'Return it to the place of purchase' may appear only as the FSIS instruction; never point her to a store. Cross-link is-boars-head-safe-to-eat-now instead of repeating the deli story. Photo set: generic (sausage links, a freezer drawer, a USDA inspection seal on a plain package) with no brand art, so it survives a retitle.

topics.title: Is Tylenol Being Recalled in 2026? What Amazon's Acetaminophen Recall Actually Covers (2026)
topics.angle: Flu season is starting. She has the big bottle of 'Tylenol' in the cabinet, often the Amazon one, and wants to know right now if it is safe to take or to give her husband.
topics.facts: openFDA drug enforcement data, queried 10/22/2026 (https://api.fda.gov/drug/enforcement.json?search=product_description:%22acetaminophen%22+AND+report_date:%5B20260801+TO+20261022%5D&limit=50). Aurobindo Pharma USA recalled Amazon-brand Acetaminophen Extra Strength 500 mg caplets, 1000 count, NDC 72288-692-01, lot ACD124048A, exp 11/30/2027, labeled Made in India. That is 7,836 bottles. The recall started Sep 18, 2026 and was reported Oct 7, 2026, after complaints of discolored tablets. It is US nationwide, voluntary, firm initiated and Not Yet Classified. The same openFDA data shows two Tylenol-brand recalls in the last 12 months. (1) Kenvue Brands recalled ONE lot of TYLENOL Extra Strength 24 caplets (NDC 50580-378-04, lot EJA022, exp 4/30/2028) for a defective container. It started 10/21/2025: Class II, 3,816 bottles, D-0121-2026. (2) Gold Star Distribution recalled all lots it distributed of Tylenol 500 mg, Cold & Flu, PM and Sinus Severe display packs, because of rodent activity at its distribution center. It started 12/26/2025: Class II, D-0277-2026. That was a distributor warehouse problem, not a Kenvue manufacturing problem. For the Amazon recall, use only 7,836 bottles and lot ACD124048A. The 112,932-bottle total and lots ACD125040A and ACD124036A from news stories are NOT in openFDA.
topics.must_fix: First line: 'No new Tylenol-brand recall in fall 2026. The bottle being recalled now is Amazon's own acetaminophen, made in India.' Then give the two smaller Tylenol-brand recalls from late 2025 with their real causes (one lot for a defective container; one distributor's warehouse stock). Add a 'Checked [date]' line and show how to find the lot number on the bottle. Discoloration is not proven harmful, so do not overstate the danger. Do not attack acetaminophen or pain relievers as a class; the villain is overseas sourcing and quality control behind a store label. FDA is the source of the recall fact, never proof that other lots are safe. No pregnancy, autism or children's hook. Never send her to a store or pharmacy.

topics.title: Are Rechargeable Hand Warmers Safe? Why HotHands Just Recalled 77,000 of Them (2026)
topics.angle: She uses one on cold mornings, or she was about to wrap them as stocking stuffers for her husband who hunts or her mom with cold hands. She wants to know if the one in her drawer can burn someone.
topics.facts: CPSC recall 27-011, Oct 1, 2026: about 77,000 HotHands Rechargeable Hand Warmers, model H163650 (batch number on the underside), sold July 2025 to Aug 2026 for $30 to $40. The lithium-ion battery can overheat and ignite. No injuries are reported. Made in China. Only electric rechargeable warmers with the white HotHands logo are included; air-activated single-use warmers are not recalled. CPSC recall 27-009, Oct 1, 2026: Gobi Heat recalled about 5,500 rechargeable hand warmers, model UT3053, sold only on GobiHeat.com Oct 2024 to Aug 2026 for $20 to $40. No injuries reported; made in China. CPSC recall 26-659, July 30, 2026: about 1.5 million OCOOPA rechargeable warmers, with 1,480 overheating reports, 15 fires, 350 burn injuries and the death of an 83-year-old consumer in San Diego, California in February 2026.
topics.must_fix: Lead with HotHands. OCOOPA is already the sidebar in are-electric-blankets-safe, so keep it to one plain sentence that includes the death, and cross-link. HotHands and Gobi Heat report no injuries; never lump them in with OCOOPA's injury count. UT3053 appears as both a Gobi Heat and an OCOOPA model number; state that as a neutral fact and do not imply a shared factory. Do not describe the person who died beyond what CPSC printed. Single-use air-activated warmers were not recalled. No child or toddler hook. Never name a store as where to shop, or a competing brand as the 'safe' one. A recalled lithium battery goes to battery disposal, not the trash. CPSC is the fact source, not proof other models are safe. No flame art on hands.

topics.title: Is Full Retirement Age Changing in November? What the 1983 Schedule Really Does Next (2026)
topics.keyword: is full retirement age changing in november

People born in 1959 reach it at 66 and 10 months, and everyone born in 1960 or later reaches it at 67, so their full benefits start in 2027, not 2026. Check the month math on SSA's table in a browser (people born on the 1st count as born in the previous month). topics.title: Why Is Turkey So Expensive This Year? What Butterball Agreed to Pay $34 Million to Settle (2026)
topics.keyword: why is turkey so expensive this year
topics.angle: She hosts Thanksgiving for 12. She saw the price of the bird and wants to know if it is bird flu, greed or both, and whether she is being played.
topics.facts: Bloomberg Law, Aug 24, 2026. Butterball LLC agreed to pay $34 million to settle turkey price-fixing claims by a certified class of DIRECT PURCHASERS (wholesale buyers) in the Northern District of Illinois (In re Turkey Antitrust Litigation; confirm docket 1:19-cv-08318 on CourtListener). The preliminary approval motion was filed Aug 21, 2026. Cargill paid $32.5 million and Prestage $15 million; with the other settlements, the class recovery would be about $130.7 million if this settlement is approved. CIDRAP (page undated; it reads as late Sept or early Oct 2026): H5N1 hit turkey flocks of 77,200 and 31,200 birds in Stearns County, MN. In the 30 days before early October, 620,000 birds were lost across 14 commercial and 7 backyard flocks.
topics.must_fix: A settlement is not a finding. Bloomberg's text does not say whether Butterball denied wrongdoing, so confirm that before writing it. The money goes to wholesale buyers; say plainly that shoppers cannot file a claim. Cite the CIDRAP numbers as 'in the 30 days before early October'. The Oct 21 Barron County, WI detection was a commercial poultry flock with no species given; do not call it turkey. Leave out the unverified Oct 9 breeder turkey case. Do not say turkey is unsafe because of bird flu. No frugal angle: no cheap turkey tips, no loss leader prices, never a grocery store. Cite USDA for counts only, never as reassurance. Same shape as why-is-beef-so-expensive and why-did-eggs-cost-so-much; cross-link them and the Riverbend beef angle.

topics.title: Are Panty Liners Safe to Wear Every Day? What the New Carefree PFAS Lawsuit Claims (2026)
topics.keyword: are panty liners safe to wear daily
topics.angle: She wears one every day for perimenopause spotting or a little leak when she laughs, against her body 8 to 10 hours. She just learned it may hold a chemical California had to ban by law, and she wants to know what to wear instead. Lead the title and first line with the search. Second search to answer in the body or FAQ: 'do panty liners contain pfas'. The villain is the companies that make and sold Carefree and the 'intentionally added' wording that can let a forever chemical slip past a state ban, never the woman wearing them.
topics.facts: Hoodline, Oct 22, 2026 (https://hoodline.com/2026/10/l-a-county-residents-sue-essity-edgewell-over-pfas-in-carefree-liners/). Hundreds of LA County residents filed suit on Oct 9, 2026 in Los Angeles County Superior Court. The defendants are Essity, Edgewell Personal Care, Johnson & Johnson and Gelson's Markets (named as a seller). Plaintiffs say a 2024 independent lab test found PFOA in one or more of the liner's five layers. They also say the liners stayed on sale after California AB 2515 took effect Jan 1, 2025; that law bans intentionally added PFAS in menstrual products (confirm the bill text and effective date on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov). An Essity spokesperson says the company 'does not intentionally add PFAS chemicals to Carefree products.' A separate 2024 lawsuit, Ecological Alliance v. Edgewell, was filed in LA Superior Court over PFOA in the same liners (Fox LA, Sept 30, 2024: https://www.foxla.com/news/carefree-panty-liners-contain-cancer-causing-forever-chemical-lawsuit-alleges). Do NOT print the caption 'Lindsey et al. v. Edgewell' until the LA Superior Court docket confirms it.
topics.must_fix: The cancer and hormone claims are allegations, not findings. Say 'the lawsuit claims' every time, and say 'hundreds of women', not an exact count. Do not say PFOA was intentionally added: Essity denies it, and the case turns on those words. Who owns Carefree is not confirmed, so say 'the companies that make and sold Carefree' until it is. Call the 2024 case 'a separate 2024 lawsuit', not a Prop 65 case. Gelson's is a defendant only as a seller; never point her to or away from any store. Keep the hook on her (perimenopause, light leaks), never on teens or daughters. No product-return wording. Cross-link is-tampax-safe as the sister story (confirm it is live). The swap is a liner from a company that says what is in every layer, described plainly, never a named rival brand.
